chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Inform me about the divorced woman for whom mu'tah (consolation gift) is obligatory upon her husband. Which one is she? For some of your followers claim that mu'tah is obligatory for the divorced woman who has been definitively divorced (bain) and her husband has no right of return (raj'ah) to her. As for the one upon whom there is a right of return, she has no mu'tah.' He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'The definitively divorced woman (al-bainah).'

key_terms.الْمُتْعَة: Mu'tah (consolation gift given to the wife upon divorce)
key_terms.رَجْعَة: Right of return (the husband's right to take back his wife during the waiting period without a new contract)

ai.seo_question: Which type of divorced woman is entitled to the consolation gift (mu'tah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hassan (AS) clarifies the specific category of divorce triggering the obligation of *mu'tah* by identifying it as *al-bainah*, thereby resolving the juristic debate among his followers regarding whether the right applies only to irrevocable divorces (*bain qubla al-dukhul*) or also to revocable ones. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on financial compensation as a distinct right of the wife independent of the husband's power of *raj'a* (reconciliation).
